Release notes

Sourced from httpx2's releases.

v2.14.0

Highlights

🌐 CIDR ranges in NO_PROXY

NO_PROXY and mounts now match IP CIDR ranges like 192.168.0.0/16 and [fe80::]/10, so any address in the range bypasses the proxy (#1165). Bracketed IPv6 addresses like [::1]:8080 are accepted, and unparseable NO_PROXY entries are ignored instead of failing client creation (#1267).

🔐 FIPS-enforced Python support

httpx2 now imports on FIPS-enforced Python builds without hashlib.md5. DigestAuth raises ProtocolError only when the server asks for an unavailable algorithm (#1130).

🔌 Sturdier connections and WebSocket shutdown

HTTP/2 reads no longer block when a server lowers SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS mid-flight (#1217), and writing after a peer closes TLS without close_notify raises WriteError (#1263). Sync WebSocket sessions no longer hang on exit with a full event queue (#1123), and ASGI WebSocket reads after app shutdown no longer leak anyio exceptions (#1233).

httpx2

Added

  • Match IP CIDR ranges, like 192.168.0.0/16 and [fe80::]/10, in NO_PROXY and mounts. Requests to any address in the range now bypass the proxy; previously only the network address itself did (#1165).
  • Accept bracketed IPv6 addresses, like [::1] and [::1]:8080, in NO_PROXY (#1267).

Changed

  • Raise InvalidURL for a mounts key with an IP host followed by anything other than a valid CIDR prefix, like all://10.0.0.0/33 (#1165).

Fixed

  • Ignore NO_PROXY entries that cannot be parsed, instead of raising InvalidURL when the client is created (#1267).
  • Import httpx2 on FIPS-enforced Python builds without hashlib.md5. DigestAuth raises ProtocolError when the server asks for an unavailable algorithm (#1130).
  • Handle reads after an ASGI WebSocket app shuts down, instead of leaking anyio exceptions (#1233).
  • Stop the sync WebSocket session from hanging on exit when its event queue is full (#1123).

httpcore2

Fixed

  • Keep CONNECT and absolute-form proxy targets when the request sets the target extension (#1262).
  • Stop blocking reads when an HTTP/2 server lowers SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS while requests are in flight (#1217).
  • Raise WriteError instead of anyio.EndOfStream when writing after the peer closes a TLS connection without close_notify (#1263).

  • Speed up snapshot conversion for literal constants, especially in large lists and dictionaries.

  • Built-in literal values are always managed; attempting to register their types as unmanaged raises TypeError.

  • Scope unmanaged type registrations to the current snapshot context, inheriting registrations from the parent context.

  • Speed up snapshot comparisons by avoiding unnecessary deep copies of immutable built-in values.

  • Speed up snapshot conversion by reading AST constant values directly instead of compiling and evaluating them.

Fixed

  • Respect show-updates in the short report, hiding snapshot representation change messages when it is disabled.

Added

  • The customize hook now receives a snapshot_value argument with the corresponding existing snapshot value, or ... when there is no corresponding snapshot.

NO_PROXY and mounts now match IP CIDR ranges like 192.168.0.0/16 and [fe80::]/10, so any address in the range bypasses the proxy (#1165). Bracketed IPv6 addresses like [::1]:8080 are accepted, and unparseable NO_PROXY entries are ignored instead of failing client creation (#1267).

pluggy 1.7.0 (2026-10-14)

Deprecations and Removals

  • [#632](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/632) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/632>_: Hookspec methods defined without self as the first parameter now emit a :class:DeprecationWarning. Add self as the first parameter or use @staticmethod.

Features

  • [#170](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/170) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/170>_: Hookspecs can now declare default values for arguments, using the usual def myhook(myarg="default") syntax.   • [#729](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/729) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/729>_: Tracing now adds detail where str() is ambiguous: empty strings and strings containing whitespace are quoted, and enums and paths show their repr().

    A value spanning several lines is now displayed as a block instead of running into the surrounding trace.

Bug Fixes

  • [#629](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/629) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/629>_: Fix hooks failing to register on Python 3.14+ when type annotations use forward references.

  • [#315](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/315) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/315>_: Source archives created by git archive (including GitHub's "Source code" downloads) now carry version information, so building pluggy from them no longer fails with a missing version.

  • [#442](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/442) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/442>_: With the addition of default values for hookspec arguments, we also changed the precedence of default values for hookimpl arguments. Previously, if a hookimpl function declared a default for an argument, it was always used, even if the hook call passed an explicit value. Now the precedence is changed to: hook call passed value > hookspec default value > hookimpl default value. See :ref:hookimpl_arg_defaults.

  • [#701](https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/701) <https://github.com/pytest-dev/pluggy/issues/701>_: Hookimpls and hookspecs are now discovered via :func:inspect.getattr_static, so properties, cached_property and other descriptors are no longer executed while scanning a plugin. Hooks declared through such a descriptor are not supported.

    As a side effect, @hookimpl/@hookspec applied above @classmethod or @staticmethod is now picked up; previously the marker sat on the wrapper where getattr() never saw it. Callables stored directly on a plugin instance -- in its __dict__ or in a __slots__ slot -- keep being called exactly as getattr() returned them, i.e. without an implicit self.

All required CI checks pass on dff32147ace9320bb2fafeddc05819883b10ec13, including Python 3.10/3.14, HTTPX2, build, lint, security scanning, and the trusted dependency-security gate. The additional browser-demo job is still installing Chromium. Prerequisite #4185 has merged. This branch is refreshed against main, retaining the previously merged Griffe 2.3.0 update and limiting dependency version changes to aiohttp, multidict, PyJWT, and yarl. Upstream behavior changes to consider for applications sharing these dependencies: aiohttp adds a default 1,000-field limit when its **server** parses URL-encoded forms (configurable via client_max_fields); yarl corrects query decoding; PyJWT tightens malformed-input handling and changes JWKS cache object reuse.   • Fixed a data race on the free-threaded build where a retired hash table's reader count used relaxed atomics, letting a lock-free get()/getone()/ __getitem__() read race a concurrent free of that table. The reader-exit decrement and the drain's free check now use release/acquire ordering instead -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1481.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where two threads calling update(), merge(), or __setitem__() on the same key at the same time could lose the key entirely instead of just racing on which value wins. A decref of the replaced value could transiently suspend the writer's critical section, letting a second writer for the same key observe the first writer's in-progress entry as absent and, once both settled, mistake it for a stale duplicate and delete it. Every such decref is now deferred until the writer has released its critical section, so the window can no longer open. setdefault() had an unrelated instance of the same blind spot (it could insert a duplicate rather than recognizing an in-flight key), fixed alongside it -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1483.

## Summary

Adds typed 12-hour Responses prompt-cache lifetimes and optional
cache-write usage details.

## Changes

- Accept "12h" alongside "30m" in Responses request and response TTL
types.
- Expose optional cache-write details with separate 30-minute and
12-hour token counts.

## Compatibility

Callers that type a returned TTL as exactly `Literal["30m"]` should
allow `"12h"` too. The optional usage breakdown now decodes as a typed
model.
